text:
nina: Quick heads-up: saw a customer incident where a tenant's route was revoked during high qps and traffic either stalled or kept hitting an old backend for ~30s. Repro guide below.

chris: Ugh. Is this TTL expiry or explicit revocation? They can be handled differently.

nina: It's explicit revocation from the policy control plane. We push new policy with "state: revoked" and the edge kept using the older manifest until its local cache TTL expired.

oscar: That suggests a stale-push window. Our router only aggressively updates on manifest_stamp bump; revocation currently piggybacks on same channel but we don't force apply it.

pat: Repro steps I used: 1) create route, 2) hit at 400rps, 3) update route -> {"state":"revoked","revoked_by":"ops","revoked_at":1620000000}, 4) observe edge behavior. Logs: `router: policy_version=7 local_version=6 -> continue` over and over.

nina: Edge logs: `WARN policy_mismatch: revocation_seen=false cached_ttl=120s` then later `INFO policy_refresh: ttl_expired` then it applies. So revocation relied on TTL.

chris: We need a faster path. Options: (A) publish revocation events to router pubsub with immediate invalidation, (B) short-circuit routers to query lease table on mismatch, (C) accept small read pressure and keep TTL tiny, or (D) two-phase drain model.

oscar: I vote for (A) + (D). Push events with acks so maestro knows router applied it. But also add a `drain_until` timestamp so we don't interrupt in-flight work.

pat: Two implementation challenges: hedged requests and pre-warmed pools. Hedged reqs could race: one leg sees revoked/draining, other doesn't. We need deterministic tie-breaker. Suggest adding request header `policy_observed_at` with the policy_revision timestamp. Router side will attach `policy_observed_at` on the outbound to backends so backends can reject if out-of-date.

nina: That makes sense. We also need an opt-in strict mode for tenants that cannot tolerate any access after revocation. Maybe `policy.meta.strict_block=true`. Default false.

chris: Good point. For strict_block=true we should short-circuit to fallback immediately and increment a `route.blocked` metric. For non-strict, we prefer SLO-conservative behavior: if no healthy fallback then prefer latency and serve via fallback route even if revoked unless strict flag set. Document this clearly.

oscar: Telemetry: add fields on each request span: prev_policy_rev, observed_policy_rev, revoked_at, drain_until, strict_block. Emit `policy.revocation_applied` event when router transitions. Also emit `policy.revocation_pending` when maestro sees no ack from N routers past timeout.

pat: Migration: older routers check manifest_stamp_version < 3 and ignore `revoked` field. We need a staged rollout: push maestro -> routers that understand revocation + pubsub -> enable a short grace window where maestro retries pushes and falls back to TTL if no acks. After majority upgrade, flip enforcement.

nina: Edge-case: what if a revocation is operator mistake and we need rollback? Maestro should support a `revert_revocation` action that sets `state: active` and a `revert_reason`. Routers must accept reverts via same channel with idempotent semantics.

chris: Implementation tasks: 1) maestro: revocation pubsub topic + ack tracking + revert API (owner: chris), 2) router: subscribe + handle `drain_until` + attach observed_policy_rev header (owner: oscar), 3) telemetry: new events & metrics (owner: pat), 4) docs + opt-in `strict_block` semantics (owner: nina).

pat: I'll add canary dashboards: ack_rate, time_to_ack_p95, requests_served_post_revocation, hedged_inconsistency_count.

devops-bot: Canary rollout scheduled: policy-maestro/revocation-pubsub -> canary at 4620001240 by chris

nina: Cool. Let's run integration sim that includes hedging and prewarm pools. If any inconsistency shows up, abort canary. Meeting Friday 09 to review sim and canary metrics. :thumbsup:
